editorial:
Imagine being a teenager in New York City during the early nineties, escaping a rough home life to find where you belong. You will meet a group of kids from all different walks of life who didn't have much but found a bond through skateboarding. This documentary takes you right into those gritty streets before the city became fancy and expensive. It feels less like a history lesson and more like hanging out with a group of rebellious friends who are just trying to survive and have fun. The vibe is raw and honest, showing you the real friendship and chaos of that era.

What really makes this work is the old footage and the honest stories from the people who were actually there. You get to see how their real lives actually inspired the famous movie Kids, which is a pretty cool twist. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow if you aren't into skate culture. If you love street art or urban history, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing where these skaters ended up as adults. You see that while some found success, others struggled with the ghosts of their past. It concludes by linking their real-life struggles to the shocking scenes in the film Kids. The ending leaves you thinking about how the city has changed and how these kids grew up far too fast, but they always had each other to lean on.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves street culture and true stories about friendship.
